about: How long sitting officeholders have served, for the careers behind the holders at the opening (OPUS-GOV, M1-14 part 2). Mean years in the office among those sitting at a point in time.

usHouseTenureYears.source: Congressional Research Service profile of the 118th Congress (2023): average length of service about 8.5 years for Representatives at the start of the Congress.

usSenateTenureYears.source: Congressional Research Service profile of the 118th Congress (2023): average length of service about 11.2 years for Senators at the start of the Congress.

stateLegislatorTenureYears.source: NCSL legislator turnover studies (roughly a quarter of seats turn over each two-year cycle, shorter in term-limited states): mean service near six years.

statewideExecutiveTenureYears.source: Governors and statewide officers commonly serve one or two four-year terms (National Governors Association former governors roster: most serve one or two terms).

localOfficialTenureYears.source: Estimated from National League of Cities city council member profiles (most members in their first or second term of two to four years); not checked against a fetched table.

minimumAgeAtFirstTerm.source: The youngest common minimum age for state legislative and local office (21 to 25 in most states; 18 in some localities).

usHouseWinnerShare.source: Average two-party share of winning U.S. House candidates in recent cycles, about 64% (MIT Election Data and Science Lab House returns; most seats are safe). Used only to record the past elections behind sitting holders.

usSenateWinnerShare.source: Average two-party share of winning U.S. Senate candidates in recent cycles, mid-to-high 50s (MIT Election Data and Science Lab Senate returns).

stateLegislatorWinnerShare.source: Ballotpedia: the average margin of victory in contested 2024 state legislative races was 27.3 points, a winner's share near 0.635.

statewideExecutiveWinnerShare.source: Governors and statewide officers usually win with mid-50s shares (NGA and state election returns, recent cycles).

localWinnerShare.source: Local incumbents usually win comfortably in low-turnout contests (Ballotpedia local election analyses); about 0.6 of the vote.

localElectionLeadDays.source: Days between a local election and the term it fills, where the term doesn't start in January (most local terms start one to two months after the election).

pastHoldersRecorded.source: How many of an office's holders before the current one the opening records, each with a career of their own: enough that an office's past is a line of different people (a player asking who held the seat before sees them), few enough to keep the opening's records small.
